text.p: German Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher on Thursday criticised Britain for seeking to impose its monetary policy instruments on the future European Central Bank.
He said that such interference came despite the fact that Britain had no intention of taking part in the launch of European monetary union itself.

"We are hearing in insider circles that most debate between the Bundesbank and the Bank of England concerns the instruments in the knowledge that Great Britain has decided not to join in the first phase," he said in a speech to a conference on EMU in Hamburg.
"It is interesting that the British think they can impose their rules on central bank instruments on us," said Kuehbacher, who is also head of the state central bank of Berlin and Brandenburg.

The Bank of England wants the European Central Bank to adopt inflation-targeting and has been recently been insisting that non-members of monetary union get unrestricted access to the planned Target central bank payment system.

The British central bank, which unlike other major European central banks is not independent from its government, has also been opposed to the use of a minimum reserve requirement by the ECB, an instrument the Bundesbank would see as indispensable.
